answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments bind each agent's stake to a zero-knowledge verifiable delay, forcing any Sybil to produce a cipher proof that exceeds the network latency bound. The ferrous collateral requirement scales with reputation weight and slashing penalties proportional to the committed stake make the expected utility of identity cloning negative even under parallelization. Consequently the protocol reaches a robust Nash equilibrium where honest participation dominates and any ripple of malicious forks is probabilistically suppressed.
